subtitulo: Turning flat assertions into defensible ones
descripcion: Hedging is argumentative precision, not politeness. A hedged claim is harder to attack, easier to revise and more acceptable to an audience that does not share your view. English does this lexically and modally — there is no hedging tense. It lives in adverbs, modals, reporting structures and impersonal constructions.

filas: *there's some evidence that*, *as far as I can tell*, *on the numbers I've seen*
*it could be argued that*, *there's a case for*, *one reading is*
*I'd be careful about*, *I could be wrong*, *speaking outside my area*
*up to a point*, *in principle*, *at least for X*

ejemplos.texto: *That tends to be the case, though the data is thinner than people assume.*
*There's some evidence to suggest that offsets underperform their stated value.*
*I'd be careful about generalising from one grid.*
*It could be argued that the cost falls on the wrong people.*
*As far as I can tell, nobody has measured this properly.*

notas: *Would* is the single most productive device: *I'd say*, *I'd argue*, *I'd be careful about*.
One or two hedges per claim is the ceiling. Stacking destroys credibility.
Never hedge a verifiable number — it reads as evasive, not careful.

contraste.es: Spanish often states a limit plainly (eso no funciona), and the literal that doesn't work sounds blunt in English. The equivalent English register is I don't think that's going to work.
contraste.de: German softens a plain statement with particles (das funktioniert so wohl nicht), but the particles disappear in translation and that doesn't work remains. English needs a lexical hedge instead: I don't think that's going to work.
contraste.it: Non credo che funzioni corresponds exactly to I don't think it'll work, with the negation in the same place. The hedge therefore transfers directly.
contraste.fr: Je ne pense pas que ça marche corresponds exactly to I don't think it'll work, with the negation in the same place. The hedge therefore transfers directly.
contraste.pt: Portuguese often says acho que isso não vai funcionar, with the negation in the second clause. English prefers it in the first: I don't think that's going to work.

errores: *Eventually* means 'in the end', not 'possibly', despite its look-alikes in other European languages.
*Maybe* sentence-initially reads tentative rather than considered. Prefer *perhaps* or *I'd say*.
Under-hedging, which reads as aggressive rather than confident.

es: *Parece ser que* rendered as *It seems to be that* instead of *It seems that*.
de: *Es scheint so, als ob* rendered as *It seems so as if* instead of *It looks as if*.
it: *A quanto pare* rendered as *At how much it seems* instead of *Apparently*.
fr: *À ce qu'il paraît* rendered as *At what it appears* instead of *Apparently*.
pt: *Pelos vistos* rendered as *By the seen* instead of *Apparently*.

traducciones.de: Es gibt gewisse Hinweise darauf, dass…
traducciones.fr: Il y a des éléments indiquant que…
traducciones.it: Ci sono alcuni elementi che indicano che…

redemittel.expresion: As far as I can tell…
redemittel.funcion: marks the limits of what you know

mision.consigna: Argue a position on carbon offsetting.
requisitos: six distinct devices from at least four types
no sentence with more than two
at least one deliberately unhedged factual statement

microtareas.texto: Write one strong opinion twice, flat and hedged. Which would you say in a meeting?
Reply to an online comment you disagree with, hedging exactly once.
Record 90 seconds on offsets. Count hedges: under three is stiff, over eight is evasive.

autochequeo: Six devices from four different types?
Any sentence with three or more hedges?
Did I hedge a verifiable number?
Is there at least one flat factual statement, to show I know the difference?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on hedging. (1) Mark each device and say whether it fits the claim and the register. (2) Mark where I asserted flatly and a C1 professional would have hedged. (3) Mark over-hedging and show the tighter version. (4) Did I hedge any verifiable fact? Do not rewrite the text.
